test_policy.notes: Haverford's admission process is "test-optional - it is entirely your choice as the applicant whether or not to submit standardized test scores"; "there is no negative impact on your application whichever choice you make." Self-reported or official SAT/ACT scores are accepted (no preference); official scores are required after enrollment. Score-reporting codes: SAT 2289, ACT 3590. Common App grid: tests never required.

requirements.notes: Common App, Coalition (Scoir) or QuestBridge application plus the Haverford Supplement (two short essays, 150-200 words each). School Report with counselor recommendation, transcript and school profile; two teacher evaluations (English, math, science, social studies or a language other than English); mid-year report; ED applicants also send the ED form and first-quarter grades by December 1 (predicted grades are enough for international students). Interviews are not required but all applicants are encouraged to interview; "Interviews are evaluative". International students may add an InitialView or Vericant interview. The $65 fee can be waived with a counselor letter. International aid applicants use the CSS Profile (Haverford's own International Student Financial Aid Application if the Profile cannot be completed) and never the FAFSA; deadlines are the same as the admission deadlines.

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding. Decision "by December 15". International students have the same deadlines as all applicants. The Common App 2026-27 grid also lists 11/15/2026.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: "Postmark your application by January 10"; decision in "early April" (no exact date published); reply by May 1. No enrollment deposit is required.

deadlines.label: Financial aid (ED I)
deadlines.notes: CSS Profile and supporting documents "as soon as possible, but no later than" this date; register with the College Board by October 15, 2026.

deadlines.label: Financial aid (ED II)
deadlines.notes: CSS Profile and supporting documents no later than this date; register with the College Board by December 1, 2026.

deadlines.label: Financial aid (RD)
deadlines.notes: CSS Profile and supporting documents no later than this date; register with the College Board by January 1, 2027. The international-applicants page gives the same three dates.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required of applicants whose first language is not English and who have never attended a secondary school where English is the primary language of instruction. One of TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic or Duolingo English Test; Haverford does not prefer one exam. Official scores are sent by the testing agency (or, if that is a financial burden, ask admission@haverford.edu); official scores are needed on matriculation. For 2026-27 Haverford accepts TOEFL iBT on either the old 0-120 or the new 1-6 scale. The Common App grid lists D, I, T (no PTE or Cambridge).

english.notes: "minimum score of 100 on the previous 0-120 scale".
"or 5 on the new 1-6 scale". For 2026-27 scores on either scale are accepted.

aid.notes: Haverford "provides financial aid to a limited number of international students each year. All of Haverford's financial aid is need-based. Those who do receive financial aid will have their demonstrated need met in full." The page does not use the words need-blind or need-aware; the admission pages also say the College "will meet 100% of your demonstrated financial need" if you apply for aid and are admitted. International students who do not receive aid in their first year are not eligible later. Aid does not cover international travel. Apply with the 2027-28 CSS Profile (code 2289), or Haverford's International Student Financial Aid Application if the Profile cannot be completed; no FAFSA. No merit scholarships: all aid is need-based.

toefl.note: From Haverford's transfer-students page ("Haverford Code #2289"); the first-year international page lists only SAT and ACT codes.

ielts.note: No numeric code published; send IELTS results to Haverford by name through the testing agency.

duolingo.note: No code published; send Duolingo results to Haverford through your Duolingo account.

tier_notes.computer_science: Small liberal-arts CS department (7.95% of 2024-25 degrees, CDS J1); no research-university CS program.
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Strong sciences for a liberal-arts college (biology 10.88% of degrees, CDS J1) but small and undergraduate-only.
tier_notes.pre_med: Strong pre-health preparation inside a small liberal-arts college; editorial judgment.
tier_notes.economics: Social sciences are the largest degree area (26.15%, CDS J1); economics is a solid but not top-10 liberal-arts program.
tier_notes.math_physics: Physical sciences 15.27% and math/statistics 7.95% of degrees (CDS J1); well-regarded liberal-arts sciences.
tier_notes.humanities: Real humanities depth (English, history, philosophy, religion, languages) but no standout rank above the college's overall level.
tier_notes.arts_design: Fine arts is a small program (visual and performing arts 2.93% of degrees, CDS J1).
tier_notes.engineering: No engineering major (CDS J1 reports no engineering degrees).
tier_notes.business: No business major (CDS J1 reports no business degrees).
